about: A non-Cuban Partagas from General Cigar that broke from the brand's usual Cameroon wrapper when it launched in 2012. It was reblended and renamed 1845 Clásico in 2017, and the maker now lists it as retired.
notes: Blend shown is the 2017 Clásico reblend. The 2012 original used an Ecuadorian Habano Viso wrapper and Connecticut Habano binder, and the maker's site still lists that older blend. Neptune lists it as medium.
verifyNotes: No changes. 2017 blend, sizes, country and factory confirmed on halfwheel and Cigar Coop; medium to full is the maker's own body rating and Holt's agrees.

about: A Cuban robusto from Habanos S.A. and the best known cigar in the Partagás Serie D range. Habanos rates the brand as full strength and blends it from Vuelta Abajo tobacco.
notes: This is one size (a 4 7/8 x 50 robusto) in the Cuban Partagás Serie D range, not a full line. It is the Cuban Partagás from Habanos S.A., a different product from the non-Cuban Partagas sold in the US. Habanos rates the brand full, while Cigar Aficionado has rated it medium. The 1975 release year comes from Wikipedia only.
verifyNotes: Set factory to null: Habanos does not name a factory for this cigar, and the factory in the researcher's halfwheel source belonged to the 2005 Reserva limited edition. Replaced that halfwheel link with a Cigar Aficionado rating of the regular cigar, which confirms 4 7/8 x 50 and Cuban tobacco. Full strength confirmed on habanos.com (Fuerte).

about: The dark, full-bodied member of the non-Cuban Partagas family, built around a late-harvested Medio Tiempo wrapper and ligero-heavy Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. It is a current core line.
notes: The maker lists the wrapper as Connecticut Havana seed Medio Tiempo, while Holt's calls it Connecticut Broadleaf. The maker's text says full bodied but its body gauge reads medium to full. Famous, Holt's and Neptune all list it as full.
verifyNotes: Fields confirmed against the maker, Famous and Holt's. Added the maker's medium to full gauge reading to notes.

about: A non-Cuban Partagas from General Cigar that was sold in the mid-2000s, with sizes named after months of the year. Cigar Aficionado lists it as Dominican made with a Honduran wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
notes: Cigar Aficionado lists this as Partagas Cifuentes Blend and rated it from 2005 to 2007. The maker's site no longer lists it. Its tasting notes call two sizes a pressed maduro, but no leaf type is published. A separate 1990s cigar, Cifuentes by Partagas, was made in Jamaica with a Connecticut Shade wrapper.
verifyNotes: Changed found from false to true. Cigar Aficionado's ratings database has a Partagas Cifuentes Blend line; wrapper, binder, filler, country, strength and sizes are taken from five of its rating pages. No maker or halfwheel page was found, so the release year and factory are null and discontinued is inferred from its absence on the maker's site.

about: The classic non-Cuban Partagas, known for its Cameroon wrapper and yellow boxes. It is made in the Dominican Republic and remains the brand's core line.
notes: The maker lists this core line simply as Partagás, and it is often called the Yellow Box line. The maker rates it mellow to medium, while Famous and Holt's list it as medium. Famous lists the Naturales at 49 ring, the maker and Holt's at 50.
verifyNotes: Fields confirmed against the maker, halfwheel, Famous and Holt's. Reworded the Naturales note to cite the maker and Holt's, which I checked.

about: A box-pressed non-Cuban Partagas released in 2018 as a tribute to five men who shaped the brand, sold in white lacquered boxes. The maker now lists it as retired.
notes: The maker rates it full bodied, Cigar Aficionado medium to full, and Neptune medium. halfwheel lists the Corona Extra Leyenda at 5 1/2 inches, while the maker and Cigar Aficionado give 5 1/4.
verifyNotes: Changed Corona Extra Leyenda length from 5.5 to 5.25: the maker's site and Cigar Aficionado's rating both give 5 1/4 x 44, against halfwheel's 5 1/2.

filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano), Honduras (Jamastran), Mexico (San Andrés)
about: A 2017 non-Cuban Partagas with a reddish Honduran wrapper, made as a look back at the brand's earlier blends. The maker now lists it as retired.
notes: halfwheel lists the Gigante as 6 x 50, while the maker and Cigar Aficionado give 6 x 60.

about: The stronger offshoot of the Partagas 1845 line, first sold in 2014 as a brick and mortar exclusive and reblended in 2017. The maker now lists it as retired.
notes: Blend shown is the 2017 reblend. The 2014 original used an Ecuadorian Habano ligero wrapper, and the maker's site still lists that older blend. The maker rates it medium to full, while Neptune lists it as full.
verifyNotes: No changes. Blend, sizes, country and factory confirmed on halfwheel and the maker's site; Neptune's full rating confirmed.

about: The darkest and fullest version of the Partagas 1845 line, first sold in 2014 through catalog and online retailers and reblended in 2017. The maker now lists it as retired.

about: Released in 2021 as the first non-Cuban Partagas with a Connecticut Shade wrapper and the first made in Nicaragua. It is the mildest cigar in the current lineup.

verifyNotes: Removed cedar from flavors: it is not in the maker's notes, halfwheel's review or the retailer descriptions I opened. Everything else confirmed.

wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of 1998 Cameroon and 2013 Connecticut Shade
about: A 2022 non-Cuban Partagas and the brand's first barber pole, pairing a 1998 Cameroon wrapper with a strip of 2013 Connecticut Shade. It is sold in limited seasonal batches in two short sizes.

verifyNotes: No changes. Confirmed against the maker and both halfwheel articles.

about: A limited non-Cuban Partagas built around a long-aged Cameroon wrapper and sold in glass tubes. General Cigar offered it from 2005 to 2009 and brought it back in 2019.

about: A 2023 non-Cuban Partagas with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over a Cameroon binder, made in Honduras. It is a current regular production line.
notes: The maker and Neptune rate it medium, while Famous lists it as full. A box-pressed Belicoso (6 1/2 x 52) was a limited size at launch.

about: One of the two debut lines from Mo Maali's Patina Cigars, released in 2017. It uses an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania tobacco and is pitched as a Connecticut with some spice up front.
